### Added
- **`components.gpu-operator`: NVIDIA's GPU operator as a chart component, off by default and independent of model serving** (giantswarm/agent-platform#327; bumblebee-plans#46, the plan's D3; epic giantswarm/giantswarm#37639). One OCIRepository + HelmRelease of Giant Swarm's gpu-operator-app — the catalog's `gpu-operator` wrapper chart on `1.x` — into `kube-system` (the release history there too, so the GPU guide's hand-installed release upgrades in place) with `crds: CreateReplace`, no `dependsOn`, `gitops.target.kubeConfig.secretRef` honoured. The operator's configuration is the new `gpu-operator:` block, forwarded under the wrapper's subchart key — a table of two rows and no third: Flatcar, driver and toolkit off (the default); nodes with a pre-installed driver, `gpu-operator.toolkit.enabled: true`. In every configuration the operator creates the `nvidia` RuntimeClass GPU pods use (`modelServing.serving.runtimeClassName: nvidia` where the platform's own release serves), so the chart adds none. One owner per cluster: with the component on, a `ClusterPolicy`, HelmRelease or App of the operator that is not this release's fails the render naming what was seen and the handover — delete cluster-manager's `<cluster>-gpu-operator` (its detection then sees the component and never re-creates it) or the hand-installed release, then switch the toggle on, or leave it off; the `ClusterPolicy` CRD is under `ownedCrds` as the backstop. The default render is unchanged but for the roster entry forwarded to connectivity (`components.gpu-operator.enabled: false`), which `make verify-target`'s golden now drops as the one difference a new component is allowed. `make verify-gpu-operator` asserts the offline half; `tests/fixtures/gpu-operator-foreign-owner.yaml` shows the refusal on a cluster; `examples/customer-bom.yaml` pins `1.3.0`. README "The GPU operator".
